body.p: This Amendment is in response to the Office Action, dated August 29, 2024 ("Office Action"). Claims 1, 4-13, 15, 16, 18-22, and 25-32 are pending, claims 2, 3, 14, 17, 23, and 24 having been canceled; claims 1, 13, 16, 18, 21, 22, 25, and 26 having been amended; claims 27- 32 having been newly added; and claims 22 and 25-28 having been withdrawn. No new matter is added. Examination of the claims in view of the ensuing remarks is respectfully requested.

Examiner rejects claims 1-4, 9-10, and 15 as allegedly being unpatentable over Pierry et al. (Pierry, US 20040186391) in view of Gupta et al. (Gupta, US 2018/0271404) for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

At page 15 of the Office Action, in response to applicant's argument that the art does not teach one breath sample recited in claim 1, the Examiner asserts that "a recitation of the intended use of the claimed invention must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art in order to patentably distinguish the claimed invention from the prior art. If the prior art structure is capable of performing the intended use, then it meets the claim." (Emphasis added.) Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Nevertheless, claim 1 has been further amended to recite a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient" and "the multiple gas sensors configured to measure concentrations of various gases including CO2, H2, H2S, and CH4 at once with the one breath sample." It is respectfully submitted that the above-identified phrase recited in amended claim 1 is not a recitation of intended use of the claimed system. Amended claim 1 clearly requires using multiple gas sensors to determine concentrations of various gases at once with one breath sample from a patient. Disclosed throughout the specification as originally filed is that a reliable determination of whether a patient has SIBO may require testing each of CO2, H2, H2S, and CH4 gases with a single exhalation of air introduced into a system. For example, see paragraphs [00101], [00111], [00112], [00132], [00134], [00135], and [00137] of the specification as originally filed.

While Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's assertion that "a recitation of the intended use of the claimed invention must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art in order to patentably distinguish the claimed invention from the prior
Page 6 of 12

art," claim 1 has been amended to advance prosecution of the present application. As amended, claim 1 further recites "wherein the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold." These features now recited in amended claim 1 were previously recited in claims 2 and 3, and thus, rejections of claims 2 and 3 are discussed here to support allowability of amended claim 1. Further support/example of the above-identified features can also be found in at least FIGS. 8-10 of the present application. Furthermore, paragraph [00132] of the specification as originally filed discloses that "the methane 1132 sensor 800 may be connected separate from the manifold, and instead may be connected with pipes to the manifold channel. This may be the case where the methane sensor is a larger and more accurate sensor and thus would not easily fit in the manifold and would not require the consistent flow rate and temperature to accurately measure the methane concentration." Thus, the claimed structure of the sensors, i.e., "the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold" recited in amended claim 1, is not obvious variants of including CH4 as a side stream or a mainstream sensor as desired in order to determine physiological conditions, contrary to the Examiner's assertion.

With regard to the rejection of claim 2, the Examiner asserts that Gupta discloses a CH4 sensor. The Examiner further asserts that FIG. 5 of Pierry discloses that sensors can either be mainstream or side stream, and it is interpreted that side stream is separate from the manifold 32. Furthermore, the Examiner asserts that the cited combination of Gupta and Pierry discloses that CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold. Applicant respectfully disagrees for the following reasons.

While the Examiner asserts that Pierry discloses multiple gas sensors comprising a CO2 sensor, the Examiner admits that Pierry does not teach that the multiple gas sensors also comprise a CH4 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor. Thus, according to the Examiner's admission, Pierry merely discloses a single gas sensor which is a CO2 sensor. Thus, according to the Examiner's assertion, the CO2 sensor, a single gas sensor allegedly disclosed in Pierry "can either be mainstream or side stream," as stated by the Examiner. Nevertheless, with regard to the rejection of claim 3, the Examiner asserts that Pierry teaches sensors including at least CO2 and other gases positioned "in series along the gas flow path and the gas flow path comprises a single channel in
Page 7 of 12

the manifold" because FIG. 5 of Pierry discloses a single channel interpreted as mainstream tube gas flow path, the sensors shown including two mainstream and one side stream sensing, and Gupta teaches the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor. In view of the Examiner's interpretation of Pierry's disclosure discussed above, even if Pierry and Gupta are combined, they cannot arrive at "wherein the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold," as recited in amended claim 1, because Gupta is silent about the structure of the multiple gas sensors.

Further, although paragraph [0041] of Pierry discloses that the respiratory gases to which the invention applies include, but are not limited to, gases associated with respiration (i.e., oxygen and carbon dioxide), gases associated with anesthesia (i.e., nitrous oxide and halogenated agents), gases associated with therapy (i.e., helium/oxygen mixtures and nitric oxide) and gases or substances present in the breath known as markers of diseases or physiological processes (i.e., nitric oxide), Pierry clearly fails to disclose or suggest that concentrations of the various gases are determined at once using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient. Gupta fails to cure the deficiency of Pierry identified above.

Pierry discloses a respiratory gas monitoring system comprising gas measurement system(s) adapted to be placed in fluid communication with an airway of a patient to measure at least one respiratory gas. See claims 1 and 8 and paragraphs [0018], [0021], and [0044] of Pierry. In particular, according to paragraph [0044] of Pierry, the sample gas is continuously aspirated from the breathing circuit or the nasal canula through sampling tube 30. Further, paragraph [0011] of Pierry discloses using a nasal canula as the gas collection element in a conventional sidestream system so that the gas is taken directly at the patient's airway. Furthermore, paragraph [0032] of Pierry discloses that a mainstream Gas Measurement System must be sufficiently small in size and lightweight as not to interfere with patient and/or ventilator management, and paragraph [0033] of Pierry discloses that an exemplary application of the mainstream Gas Measurement System for carbon dioxide is monitoring an intubated patient receiving mechanical ventilation, and Sample Cell 10 is placed between an endotracheal tube 62 inserted into the patient's trachea and the wye portion of breathing circuit 12 connected to a mechanical ventilator. Also see FIG. 4 of Pierry.
As amended, claim 1 further recites "a mouthpiece into which the patient blows" and "a breath collector configured to receive the patient's breath through the mouthpiece coupled to the
Page 8 of 12

breath collector." In view of the above discussion of Pierry's disclosure, it is respectfully submitted that Pierry fails to provide a motivation to combine the respiratory gas monitoring system taking gas directly at the patient's airway with a mouthpiece into which the patient "blows." Therefore, it is respectfully submitted that Pierry fails to disclose or suggest a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient, the system comprising: a mouthpiece into which the patient blows; a breath collector configured to receive the patient's breath through the mouthpiece coupled to the breath collector," as recited in amended claim 1.

Even if the asserted teachings by Pierry and Gupta are combined, they fail to disclose or teach each and every element of the above-identified and discussed features recited in amended claim 1. Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

Examiner rejects claims 1, 5, 11-14, and 16-17 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dennis et al. (Dennis, US 2017/0074857) in view of Gupta for reasons of record. Examiner rejects claims 6-8 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dennis in view of Gupta, and further in view of Saatchi et al. (Saatchi, US 2013/0165810) for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

Dennis discloses a medication adherence monitoring device configured to identify and/or quantitate volatile compounds in a gas sample. The device of Dennis includes at least one sensor adapted for identification and/or quantitation of a volatile compound of interest present in the gas sample and at least one capture device which captures volatile compounds in the gas sample. The sensor of Dennis is selected from metal oxide sensors (MOS sensors), infrared sensors (IR), Surface Acoustic Wave sensors (SAW sensors) or the like. The capture device of Dennis is selective in that, while it is efficient at capture of volatile compounds, especially volatile organic compounds, it either does not capture at all or is inefficient in the capture of moisture, hydrogen, nitrogen, or carbon dioxide, present in the gas sample, and these latter components (hydrogen and carbon dioxide) in the gas sample, therefore, merely flow through the capture device and are vented to the atmosphere. See paragraph [0024] of Dennis.
Page 9 of 12

Nevertheless, at pages 8-9 of the Office Action, the Examiner cites Gupta to cure the admitted deficiency of Dennis with regard to multiple gas sensors comprising a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor. However, as discussed above, Dennis teaches away from employing at least a CO2 sensor and an H2 sensor in the medication adherence monitoring device.

Therefore, Dennis and Gupta cannot combined to arrive at a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient," "the multiple gas sensors configured to measure concentrations of various gases including CH4, CO2, H2, and H2S at once with the one breath sample, each gas sensor configured to output sensor data relating to a concentration of a different gas passing through the gas flow path, wherein the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor," and "wherein the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold," as recited in amended claim 1. Even if the asserted teachings by Dennis and Gupta are combined, they fail to disclose or teach each and every element of the above-identified features recited in amended claim 1. Saatchi fails to cure the above- identified deficiencies of Dennis and Gupta with respect to amended claim 1.

Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

Examiner rejects claims 1, 18-19, and 21 as allegedly being unpatentable over Gupta in view of Dennis for reasons of record. Examiner rejects claim 20 as allegedly being unpatentable over Gupta in view of Dennis, and further in view of Pimentel et al. (Pimentel, WO 2018/156937 Al) for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

As discussed above, Dennis teaches away from employing at least a CO2 sensor and an H2 sensor in the medication adherence monitoring device. Thus, even if Gupta discloses multiple gas sensors comprising a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor, as asserted by the Examiner, Gupta and Dennis cannot be combined to arrive at the claimed system comprising, among others, "the multiple gas sensors configured to measure concentrations of various gases including CH4, CO2, H2, and H2S at once with the one breath sample, each gas sensor configured
Page 10 of 12

to output sensor data relating to a concentration of a different gas passing through the gas flow path, wherein the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a C02 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor," as recited in amended claim 1.

Even if the asserted teachings by Gupta and Dennis are combined, they fail to disclose or teach, "wherein the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the C02 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold," as recited in amended claim 1. Pimental fails to cure the above-identified deficiencies of Gupta and Dennis with respect to amended claim 1.

Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

p.u: oinder of All Previously Withdrawn Claims

body.p: As discussed above, amended independent claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable. Withdrawn independent claim 22 has been amended to depend from claim 1. Thus, all limitations of allowable claim 1 are present in claim 22 and its dependent claims 23-26. Therefore, there would not be a serious burden on the Examiner to examine amended claims 22-26. Applicant respectfully requests that the restriction requirement between inventions Groups I and II, as set forth in the Office action mailed on February 22, 2023, be withdrawn and claims 22-26 be rejoined and fully examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.

All of the claims in the application are now believed to be allowable. Favorable consideration and a Notice of Allowance are earnestly solicited. If questions remain regarding this application, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at (213) 629-6000.
